s: Which one of the following planets has the largest number of natural satellites or moons?
x:
Jupiter had the most moons when this was asked (63 v. Saturn's 61-62 in 2009-11) — now Saturn, 285 moons v. Jupiter's 101 (Minor Planet Center, March 2026)
Saturn has the most moons (285 v. Jupiter's 101, March 2026). In 2009 Jupiter led (63 v. 61–62), so the printed key Jupiter was right then (now Saturn).

s: Which of the following planets is the farthest planet of the solar system –
o: Some times Neptune and some times Pluto
x:
key was 'sometimes Neptune, sometimes Pluto' while Pluto was a planet — now Neptune, since Pluto became a dwarf planet (IAU, August 2006)
Neptune is the farthest planet. When this was set (2002) the key was 'sometimes Neptune and sometimes Pluto' (Pluto was inside Neptune's orbit 1979-1999), but Pluto has been a dwarf planet since August 2006 (now Neptune).

s: Which planet takes the longest period in revolving around the Sun ?
x:
Pluto was keyed as the planet with the longest year in 2004 — now Neptune (164.9 yr), Pluto being a dwarf planet since August 2006 (IAU)
Of the planets offered, Neptune has the longest year (164.9 years). Pluto (247.9 years) was the 2004 key, but it has been a dwarf planet since 2006 (now Neptune).

s: Which is the smallest planet of the solar system ?
x:
Pluto was the smallest planet when this was asked (1991) — now Mercury, since Pluto became a dwarf planet (IAU, August 2006)
Mercury (4,879 km) is now the smallest planet. In 1991 Pluto was keyed as smallest, but Pluto has been a dwarf planet since 2006 (now Mercury).

s: The number of the planet in the solar system is –
x:
9 planets until the IAU decision of August 2006 — now 8 planets, Pluto a dwarf planet (IAU 2006; Rocket General Geography #1 p.2)
In 1992 the solar system had 9 planets (now 8: Pluto became a dwarf planet in August 2006).

s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh:
1. Its coastline is about 974 km long.
2. It lies wholly between the Equator and the Tropic of Cancer.
3. Its northern limit is about 22°N.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x:
statement 1 uses the old 974 km figure — now 1,053.07 km (2025 re-measurement; NextGen Rocket AP Geography #12)
AP lies wholly between the Equator and the Tropic of Cancer, and its coastline was long given as about 974 km (now 1,053.07 km); its northern limit is 19°07'N, not 22°N.

s:
Consider the following statements.

I. The axis of the Earth’s magnetic field is inclined at 23 and half to the geographic axis of the Earth.

II. The Earth’s magnetic pole in the Northern hemisphere is located on a peninsula in Northern Canada.

III. Earth’s magnetic equator passes through Thumba is South India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x:
the north magnetic pole is no longer in northern Canada — now in the Arctic Ocean near 86°N, drifting towards Siberia (World Magnetic Model 2025)
Statement I is wrong (magnetic axis ~11.5°, not 23½°). II and III were the UPSC key: the north magnetic pole was then placed on a peninsula of northern Canada (Boothia, 1831) and the magnetic equator passes near Thumba (now the pole has drifted into the Arctic Ocean, ~86°N in 2025).

s:
Which of the following statements regarding global warming are correct?
1. Melting of polar ice caps and subsequent rise in the sea level is the most important effect of global warming
2. The sea-level is likely to rise by one meter by 2070 A.D. if the present level of global warming is not controlled
3. All the coral islands in the world will be submerged
4. By 2044 A.D, Fiji is likely to be submerged and the rise in the sea level by the same year will pose a grave danger to the Netherlands
Codes :
x:
Book key: 1, 3 and 4. Strictly only 1 holds; 'all coral islands submerged' and 'Fiji submerged by 2044' are exaggerations.
early forecasts of submerged coral islands and Fiji by 2044 — now IPCC AR6 projects 0.28–1.01 m of sea-level rise by 2100 and Fiji is not submerged (IPCC AR6, 2021)
Book key (c): melting polar ice and sea-level rise is the main effect (1), with coral islands and Fiji threatened (3, 4); statement 2 (1 m by 2070) is rejected. These were 2002-era forecasts, not facts.
